SEB-301: match each section's data file by heading text, not position (#598)

Second reviewer, two findings on PR #594:

1. sending-money.md's step-by-step (fee legs) and day-by-day (hour-by-hour chart) sections had their files swapped:
   step-by-step was citing routes_hourly.json, day-by-day was citing routes_breakdown.json. Checked against each
   file's own "definition" field: routes_breakdown.json holds the five fee legs (deposit, buy, on-chain, sell,
   withdrawal) that sum to the step-by-step table; routes_hourly.json holds the hour-by-hour time series the chart
   draws. Fixed: swapped back.

2. countries.md's four price-band sections (and home's movers/findings sections, found independently, same bug) do
   not render at all when empty that hour (bandSection() returns null, js/countries_page.js), so a position-based
   map silently shifts every section after an empty one, and source_pairs.json could attach to the wrong section or
   be dropped. The position scheme could not be made safe; replaced it with matching by the heading's own text
   (SECTION_FILES is now {page: {hero, patterns: [(regex, files), ...]}}, tried against each heading as it is
   read). Table headers (SECTION_HEADERS) matched the same way, for the same reason.

Verified: self-test covers both regressions directly (a missing band, and the step/day-by-day order) plus a real
build against live data -- confirmed the step-by-step table cites routes_breakdown.json, the chart cites
routes_hourly.json, and countries.md's no-price section (its bands are 7/13/29/10 this hour, "below" empty) cites
both index_latest.json and source_pairs.json. Script only, per CLAUDE.md: the twins are generated, never committed.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SEB-301: machine view twins, six fixes (#594)

1. Each section links only its own data file (SECTION_FILES, by the order headings appear), never all 8 the page loaded.
   A country or finding page falls back to its own one file only if it linked none itself (a held-back country with no
   raw-file table).
2. A table whose page shows no column label, or only a partial one (an axis label on one column), gets a real header
   (SECTION_HEADERS), only when the column count matches.
3. A "Show all" / "Show more" / "Show earlier" / "Show why" button is clicked before the markdown is read, so a twin
   never stops at the first 20 rows a reader would have to click through -- every priced country, and every no-price
   country with its reason.
4. An internal link to a page that has a markdown twin now points at the twin, never the .html page. A page with no
   twin (agent-incidents.html, tape.html) is left as it was, since there is nothing else to link.
5. Sentences starting "Tap" are dropped from the markdown text only; the page itself is untouched.
6. "Prices from the HH:MM UTC hour, D Mon." is now plain text under the title, not an HTML comment. The idempotency
   check (skip an hour already written) now looks for this line instead.

Script only. The twins and llms.txt are generated files; they are never committed in a PR, the next hourly collect.yml
run rebuilds them with this fixed script. Ran a full local build to verify (not committed): 72 twins, 0 failures.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
